payload.body:
Your taste, judgment, and the care you bring to what you make, choose, or support can become part of what people remember about you. What you value becomes visible through the standards you keep returning to and the choices you are willing to stand behind.

That can make people seek out your opinion. They ask what you think, invite you back because they like having you involved, or trust you with the part where presentation, tone, or the quality of the exchange actually matters.

Being well received gets complicated when the role that earns the strongest response stops reflecting what you actually value. You keep saying yes because people appreciate you there, stay attached to something because it looks good from the outside, or accept praise as proof that the choice still fits.

Being appreciated and valuing the role are different things. What you become known for should still reflect what you actually care about, not only what other people have learned to praise you for.
